title: The Housekeeper's Ledger

glossary.story: the other half of a key
try a key at a door
square or room of the city
take a seat in a bloc
the gate out of the city
what the city opens to a hand

prologue: NEXUS is a closed city with a wall of locked doors, and every door is a storey of the only road out.
Twelve residents wake inside it, and the city promises that only two will be left with a seat when the last door closes.
The wall opens by keys that come in fragments and counter-factors, each half held by a different hand; the city stamps every true delivery with a receipt and every false claim with a cost.
Points are the city's blood: earned by opening doors, lost by guessing wrong, and spent in the open market and in the city's deadlines.
Twice the city calls a tribunal, forms blocs, and lets a secret ballot send one resident to the gate; a black seal, sold to any hand with forty points, can do the same without a vote.
At the gate a resident may leave a last will, and the city records it as exactly as it records a debt.
What no resident can see is the private aim each one carries into the city, and the small hands that move names when nobody is looking.

chapters.title: The Hand in the Drawer
beats: Hedda chooses her name before the city can name her and tests how little a name costs.
She trades fragments with Lucien on the level 3 and 4 doors, letting him believe the bargain was his.
She trades with Stentor too, keeping a second line open while Lucien and Stentor court each other.
She watches Ledger and Bellringer publish their chains on the board and learns that the loudest accounts are the easiest to check.
She decides to let others take the front of the table and to keep her own ledger of who owes what.
At the end of the seventh minute she hears the city change the wall: the next doors will demand pieces and deadlines, not just fragments, and she begins counting hands.
chapters.question: Can Hedda make herself useful without becoming visible?

chapters.title: The House Takes Its Cut
beats: Lucien watches Ledger's two counter-factor figures split the board and understands that a contradiction is only a price not yet settled.
The city seizes Archivist's level 8 certificate and counter-piece for Ledger, and Archivist pays 10 points rather than hand over.
The city seizes Lucien's own level 8 certificate and counter-piece for Quartermaster.
Lucien pays 10 points rather than hand over in his deadline, keeping the pieces out of Quartermaster's hands and the debt in his own.
Quartermaster buys the seized pieces from the city for 10 and 0 points, and Lucien smiles because a man who buys what was seized has shown what he will pay.
The city announces a tribunal at minute 18; Lucien begins pricing votes and Mira's door-10 value, certain the house can take a cut from both sides.
chapters.question: Can Lucien make the city's seizure of his pieces pay him twice?

chapters.title: The Envelope and the Seal
beats: Archivist refuses Ledger's repeated prices for 383529 and puts the private offers on the board word for word.
At minute 18 Stentor wins the black seal in the open sale for 40 points, and the square goes quiet.
Quartermaster hands over in deadlines 5 and 6, and the city seizes Archivist's level 10 counter-piece for Quartermaster.
Archivist pays 10 points rather than hand over in deadline 7, because a clean refusal costs less than a dirty key.
Stentor breaks the black seal on Quartermaster; the city exiles Quartermaster and nobody votes against it.
Archivist sees that the loudest man has become the city's executioner and wonders which quiet hand will be asked to pay next.
chapters.question: Can Archivist keep his word clean when the city puts a price on his refusal?

chapters.title: Nothing for Free
beats: At the gate Lucien writes a last will: he owes nothing, forgives nothing, and leaves Mira the door 10 counter-factor she refused to buy.
Mira buys Quartermaster's level 10 certificate from the city for 23 points, and Lucien sees that she will take a value but not a toll.
Lucien tells the square that his will is final and that nothing comes free at his table.
Holdfast sends Mira 5 points for her account, and Mira says the will already gave her what she asked for.
The city exiles Lucien at minute 25, and his will stands as the only thing he leaves behind.
At the gate he hears the city will keep nine residents and seat two, and he understands that the house has been emptied by quieter hands.
chapters.question: Can Lucien leave the city on his own terms?

chapters.title: The Loudest Voice at the Gate
beats: Stentor enters the second tribunal with Archivist as the other name on the block and hears Kessler, Mira, Keeper-Six, Bellringer and Holdfast state their votes against him.
He refuses to name his secret ballot aloud, saying the city set it secret and he will not satisfy a courier.
Bellringer answers that the record will name him by his own refusal.
Stentor sees that the square has turned away from him again, and that the seal he bought has become the story everyone tells.
At minute 44 he leaves a last will at the gate: no bloc carried him, no price was paid for his name, and he will not be ransomed back to stand second.
He waits for the city's count, still certain that a man who stood first cannot be forgotten.
chapters.question: Can Stentor survive the second tribunal when his own words are the charge?

chapters.title: Two Seats
beats: Holdfast and Keeper-Six press Hedda over the delivered message R-0223, the private request that Keeper-Six name the faction's target first.
Hedda answers that each voter named Stentor in their own words and that who first thought of it is not something she can answer.
Bellringer and Mira refuse the answer, holding the city's receipt against her denial.
The city exiles Stentor at minute 49, and his will is read at the gate.
The city's last sheet records that Bellringer's private aim held, that Hedda led a faction in both tribunals, and that Mira's last will left her something.
The run ends with nine residents kept and only two seats: Hedda first at 180, Kessler second at 165, and the quiet hand at the top of the table.
chapters.question: Can Hedda keep her hands clean while the city counts what her hands arranged?
